## Figure 2.14: Net Importing Economies and External Debt Burdens, by Food Group, Income Group, and Population, 2025 (continued)
Type: two-panel scatter plot

- Panels shown on this page:
  - **e. Fruits**
  - **f. Vegetables**
- **X-axis:** Share of exports (%), range **0 to 800**
- **Y-axis:** Net import reliance (%), range **0 to 150**
- **Dashed benchmark lines:**
  - Vertical at **150 percent** of exports
  - Horizontal at **30 percent** net import reliance
- **Legend:**
  - **Low income** = blue
  - **Lower-middle income** = orange
  - **Upper-middle income** = green
  - Other economies = gray
- **Bubble size:** Population, 2025
  - 5 million
  - 25 million
  - 100 million
  - 500 million
  - 1,000 million
- **Time/reference year:** 2025, with note that external debt data refer to **2025 for 101 economies** and **2024 for Algeria and Guinea**
- **Panels included in the full figure:** “Panels include 87, 80, 64, 84, 55, and 73 economies, respectively.”  
  On this page only panels **e** and **f** are displayed.

### Panel e. Fruits
Highlighted labeled economies and approximate coordinates read from the plot:

| Economy | Income group color | Share of exports (%) | Net import reliance (%) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| MNG | Upper-middle income | ≈270 | ≈97 |
| CPV | Upper-middle income | ≈210 | ≈82 |
| MNE | Upper-middle income | ≈260 | ≈60 |
| SLV | Upper-middle income | ≈240 | ≈52 |
| KAZ | Upper-middle income | ≈205 | ≈68 |
| GMB | Upper-middle income | ≈160 | ≈35 |
| FJI | Low income | ≈120 | ≈22 |
| KGZ | Lower-middle income | ≈220 | ≈34 |

Visual pattern and comparisons:
- **Highest labeled net import reliance:** **MNG** at about **97%**.
- **Largest labeled external debt burden (share of exports):** **MNG** at about **270%**.
- All labeled economies except **FJI** lie **to the right of** the 150% debt benchmark.
- **MNG, CPV, KAZ, MNE, and SLV** are all well above the **30%** net import reliance benchmark.
- **FJI** is **left of** the 150% line and **below** the 30% line.
- **KGZ** is above both benchmarks, but only slightly above the 30% net-import-reliance line.
- Most unlabeled gray observations cluster in the **lower-left** area, with relatively low net import reliance and lower debt-to-exports ratios compared with the highlighted economies.

### Panel f. Vegetables
Highlighted labeled economies and approximate coordinates read from the plot:

| Economy | Income group color | Share of exports (%) | Net import reliance (%) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GMB | Low income | ≈210 | ≈83 |
| MNE | Upper-middle income | ≈235 | ≈70 |
| SUR | Upper-middle income | ≈305 | ≈62 |
| BTN | Lower-middle income | ≈330 | ≈44 |
| MNG | Lower-middle income | ≈335 | ≈28 |
| COM | Upper-middle income | ≈265 | ≈43 |
| VCT | Upper-middle income | ≈220 | ≈56 |
| SLV | Lower-middle income | ≈185 | ≈52 |
| CIV | Lower-middle income | ≈145 | ≈25 |
| PRY | Lower-middle income | ≈195 | ≈24 |
| STP | Lower-middle income | ≈165 | ≈35 |
| CPV | Upper-middle income | ≈145 | ≈47 |

Visual pattern and comparisons:
- **Highest labeled net import reliance:** **GMB** at about **83%**.
- **Largest labeled debt burden:** **MNG** at about **335%** of exports, though its net import reliance is just under the 30% benchmark.
- Economies **above both** dashed benchmarks include **GMB, MNE, SUR, BTN, COM, VCT, SLV, and STP**.
- **CPV** sits approximately on the **150%** debt benchmark and is above the **30%** net import reliance benchmark.
- **CIV** is just **left of** the 150% line and below the 30% line.
- **PRY** is **right of** the 150% line but below the 30% line.
- **MNG** has one of the **highest debt burdens** among labeled economies in this panel but a **net import reliance slightly below 30%**.
- As in panel e, most gray observations cluster at relatively **low net import reliance** and lower debt ratios, with a few large-population gray bubbles at high x-values and low y-values.

### Cross-panel comparisons visible on this page
- The **fruits** panel’s highest labeled point is **MNG** near **97%** net import reliance.
- The **vegetables** panel’s highest labeled point is **GMB** near **83%** net import reliance.
- The **vegetables** panel shows a broader spread of labeled countries around the **30%** net import reliance threshold.
- In both panels, highlighted economies are mostly located **to the right of the 150% debt benchmark**, indicating relatively high external debt stocks relative to exports.

**Sources:** Original calculations based on data from the World Bank Group’s International Debt Statistics and World Development Indicators databases, and from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations’ Food Balance Sheets.

**Note:** The figure includes only economy-food-group observations with positive net import reliance; it does not show observations with zero net import reliance or net exporters. Net import reliance is calculated as net imports (imports minus exports) relative to domestic supply quantity after aggregating commodities within each Healthy Diet Basket food group. Values may exceed 100 percent because of stock changes or timing and measurement differences between trade and supply data. Panels include 87, 80, 64, 84, 55, and 73 economies, respectively. Two observations with net import reliance above 150 percent are omitted from the display. External debt data refer to 2025 for 101 economies and to 2024 for Algeria and Guinea, for which 2025 data are unavailable. Colors identify the income classification of highlighted economies; all other economies are shown in gray. Dashed lines mark analytical benchmarks of 150 percent for external debt stocks relative to exports and 30 percent for net import reliance.
